title: Essential property; creatures beatific good; glory
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Psalm 19:1. Exodus; Luke 2:9; or through opposed plus split darkness, or through production belonging toward works that same which agree with His perfection plus excellence — Matthew 17:2,5; — and that same either through unusual flashing plus shining belonging toward light plus splendor. 6:15. 1 Timothy 1:11; Deuteronomy 32; Psalm 8; 9:5; but with a certain respect outwardly, because He variously manifests His excellence above all things plus His infinite perfection by means belonging toward external acts — Romans 1:23; — and so this attribute stands as indeed out from Gods perfection. on account belonging toward His infinite perfection, He excels all things — glory stands as that same by means belonging toward which. III. And it stands as glory or joy. But ye act stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which we enjoy ye good. For ye object stands as ye good that same which we enjoy. in that same which two ye creatures blessedness consists plus shines — and yet it stands as ye beatific good belonging toward intelligent creatures by means belonging toward reason belonging toward ye object completing ye act tending into ye object plus resting in ye same. Psalm 16:2,11. 6:15; 1 Timothy 1:11; 1 Corinthians 15:28; Jeremiah; indeed ye essence itself, that same which can be communicated to no creature — Isaiah 42:8; — but Gods blessedness stands as an essential property.
pass_b_english: But Gods blessedness is an essential property, indeed the essence itself, which can be communicated to no creature — Isaiah 42:8; Jeremiah; 1 Corinthians 15:28; 1 Timothy 1:11; 6:15; Psalm 16:2,11. And yet it is the beatific good of intelligent creatures by reason of the object completing the act tending into the object and resting in the same, in which two the creatures blessedness consists and shines. For the object is the good which we enjoy. But the act is that by which we enjoy the good.

And it is glory or joy. III. Glory is that by which, on account of His infinite perfection, He excels all things. And so this attribute is indeed from Gods perfection, but with a certain respect outwardly, because He variously manifests His excellence above all things and His infinite perfection by external acts — Romans 1:23; 9:5; Psalm 8; Deuteronomy 32; 1 Timothy 1:11; 6:15.

And that either through unusual flashing and shining of light and splendor, or through opposed and split darkness, or through production of works which agree with His perfection and excellence — Matthew 17:2,5; Luke 2:9; Exodus; Psalm 19:1.
source_text: Est autem beatitudo Dei essentialis proprietas, imo ipsa essentia, quae nulli creaturae communicari potest — Isaia XLII.8; Jerem.; I Cor. XV.28; I Tim. I.11; VI.15; Psal. XVI.2,11. Et est tamen creaturarum intelligentium bonum beatificum ratione objecti destituens actus in objectum tendentis, inque eodem acquiescentis, in quibus duobus creaturae beatitudo consistit ac relucet. Objectum enim est bonum, quo fruimur. Actus vero, quo bono fruimur. Estque gloria aut gaudium. III. Gloria est, qua ob infinitam perfectionem suam omnia excellit. Atque ita hoc attributum est quidem a perfectione Dei, sed cum respectu quodam ad extra, quia excellentiam supra omnia et perfectionem suam infinitam actibus externis varie manifestat — Rom. I.23; IX.5; Psal. VIII; Deut. XXXII; I Tim. I.11; VI.15. Idque vel per luminis splendorisque inusitatam coruscationem et effulgescentiam, vel per oppositam et fissam tenebrositatem, vel per productionem operum, quae ipsius perfectioni et excellentiae congruunt — Matth. XVII.2,5; Luc. II.9; Exod.; Psal. XIX.1.
